segments.say: Setup: sheet clamped above the mould. A flat thermoplastic sheet is clamped in a frame above a mould on the machine bed, with a heater panel overhead, and the mould rises toward the sheet to start the cycle. Point at the clamped sheet on your student notes diagram before anything is heated.
questions: Which parts of the machine can you name in scene 1, and what does each one do?
Why must the sheet be clamped before the cycle starts?

segments.say: Heating: the sheet softens and sags. The heater warms the clamped sheet until the plastic becomes pliable and sags under its own weight, ready to be formed. Now try the heating questions on your worksheet.
questions: What change in the sheet tells you it is ready to be formed?
Is the sheet formed yet at this stage, and how do you know?

segments.say: Vacuum forming: air pressure pushes the sheet onto the mould. The mould rises into the soft sheet and the pump removes the air trapped beneath it, so outside air pressure, now unopposed, pushes the sheet down onto every surface of the mould. Check the forming stage against your student notes before moving on.
questions: What does the vacuum pump actually do at this stage?
What pushes the sheet onto the mould, and why can it push only after the air is removed?

segments.say: Cooling and release: the rigid shell lifts off. The formed sheet cools on the mould and sets rigid, the shell is lifted off, and the excess edge is trimmed away. Keep the clamp, heat, form, cool order as you check your student notes and finish the exit ticket.
questions: Why must the sheet cool on the mould before it is lifted off?
What are the four stages of the cycle, in order?
segments.watchFor: The vacuum sucks and pulls the soft plastic sheet down onto the mould. Listen for students who give the vacuum a pulling force it cannot have. Send them back to scene 3 and the outside air pressure label: The flat sheet is clamped in the frame and heated until pliable, the mould rises into the soft sheet, the vacuum then removes the air trapped beneath it, and the unopposed outside air pressure pushes the sheet onto every surface of the mould, where it cools, sets rigid, and is lifted off and trimmed.
